events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Tampere, Finland, as Ulrika Wilhelmina Johnson.

evidence.quote: born Ulrika Wilhelmina Johnson , 19 March 1844
Canth was born in Tampere to Gustaf Vilhelm Johnsson

events.text: Family relocated to Kuopio when father took charge of Finlaysons shop.

evidence.quote: In 1853 his father was given charge of Finlaysons textile shop in Kuopio and the entire family relocated there

events.text: Began studies at the newly founded Jyväskylä Teacher Seminary.

evidence.quote: In 1863 she began her studies at the recently founded Jyväskylä Teacher Seminary

events.text: Married her natural sciences teacher Johan Ferdinand Canth.

evidence.quote: In 1865 she married her natural sciences teacher , Johan Ferdinand Canth

events.text: Had to drop out of the Seminary after marrying.

evidence.quote: In 1865 she married her natural sciences teacher , Johan Ferdinand Canth ( 1835–1879 ) , and had to drop out of the Seminary

events.text: Canths forced to leave Keski-Suomi newspaper after controversy.

evidence.quote: In 1876 the Canths were forced to leave the paper

events.text: Employed by the competing newspaper Päijänne.

evidence.quote: they were , however , both employed by the competing Päijänne the following year

events.text: First works of fiction published in the pages of Päijänne.

evidence.quote: Minna published her first works of fiction on the pages of Päijänne

events.text: First book, Novelleja ja kertomuksia, a collection of short stories, published.

evidence.quote: compiled in her first book , Novelleja ja kertomuksia , in 1878

events.text: Husband Johan Ferdinand Canth died, leaving her a widow.

evidence.quote: her husband Johan died in 1879

events.text: Play Työmiehen vaimo (The Workers Wife) written and premiered.

evidence.quote: Minna Canths most important works are the plays Työmiehen vaimo ( The Workers Wife ) from 1885

events.text: Daughter Hanna died.
Play Anna Liisa written.

evidence.quote: Anna Liisa , penned in 1895

events.label: death
events.text: Died suddenly of a heart attack at her home in Kuopio, aged 53.

evidence.quote: Canth died suddenly of a heart attack at the age of 53 on May 12 , 1897 at her home in Kuopio

events.text: Daughter Anni died.
Son Jussi died.
Daughter Maiju died.
Daughter Elli died.
Son Pekka died.
Daughter Lyyli died.
English translation of The Burglary and The House of Roinila published by Aspasia Books.

evidence.quote: Translated into English by Richard Impola . Aspasia Books , Beaverton 2010

undated_mentions: began writing career at the newspaper Keski-Suomi (before 1876)
attended school at Finlaysons factory intended for workers' children
attended various girls' schools in Kuopio
